steps.question: What should control corners say?
steps.why: Pill controls feel playful.
Labels stay readable on vivid color.
Most visitors arrive on phones, and a compact control is too small for a thumb.
Pills match the brand's round, playful shapes. Sharp corners would feel corporate.

steps.pick: size.52
space.28

radius.pill: We use a pill corner for buttons and inputs in order to mark their role as controls in a playful tone, by brand convention. A full radius does this by rounding both ends into a capsule, the brand's signature shape. So every action feels bold and friendly, because the brand is bold (brand.q1), controls are pills (shape.values) and each section holds one big idea (content.q2).
neutral.600: the quietest text that still reads, 7.02:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: neutral.400: the quietest text that still reads, 6.71:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.

steps.question: What rises above the page?
steps.why: Cards lift to feel like objects.

steps.question: How soft are shadows?
steps.why: Pronounced shadows add depth.
Strong depth shows a menu or dialog sits above vivid sections. Without a shadow it blends into the color blocks.

steps.rule: Fills that float above content. In dark, one step lighter than content, so height reads by tone.
steps.pick: neutral.0, the same as content (surface.default): a menu stands out by its edge and its one shadow, not by its fill.
steps.darkPick: neutral.100: We use one step lighter than content for menus, dialogs and raised cards in dark, in order to show height by tone, 1.21:1 on surface.default. The lighter fill does this by the dark-mode depth rule: the higher a layer sits, the lighter its surface. So visitors see a menu above the page even where its shadow barely shows, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and the roles answer names the layers that rise (elevation.roles).

steps.pick: shadow.overlay: We use step 2 of the shadow scale for menus and dialogs in order to show floating height, one step above the cards. The cast shade does this by a 24px offset and a 48px blur at 20%, larger than the card's. So a menu sits clearly above vivid sections and cards, because cards and overlays rise (elevation.roles) and shadows are pronounced (elevation.values).
steps.darkPick: shadow.overlay-dark: We use the light overlay shadow's shape in dark in order to show the same floating height by the dark-shade relation. The cast shade does this by the same 24px offset and 48px blur, at 60% black instead of 20%. So a menu still sits above dark sections, though its shade reads weaker on dark than in light, because cards and overlays rise (elevation.roles) and dark ships as standard (theming.values).

steps.pick: radius.24: We use a 24px corner for cards, menus and dialogs in order to make each offer read as a separate object, in a bold tone by brand convention. A large radius does this by breaking the outline with a wide curve while the sides stay straight. So each offer reads as one friendly object, because containers get their own corner (shape.count) and the brand is bold (brand.q1).

steps.rule: The 1px edge of a raised layer. In dark, a solid step lighter than the raised surface, so the edge shows where a shadow cannot.
steps.pick: neutral.200: We use the default line's step for the edge of menus, dialogs and other raised layers, in order to give separation between a layer and what lies under it. The ring does this by a 1px line, 1.32:1 on surface.raised, beside the light shadow that does most of the lift. So visitors see where a menu ends on any page, because raised layers keep an edge (elevation.definition) and a decorative line has no contrast floor (accessibility.definition).
steps.darkPick: neutral.200: We use the step above the raised surface for a 1px ring around raised layers in dark, in order to give separation where a shadow barely shows. The ring does this by a solid, lighter line, 1.39:1 on surface.raised (#4D3A33, no alpha), so its contrast can be checked. So visitors see a dark menu's edge on any page, because dark ships as standard (theming.values), raised layers keep an edge (elevation.definition) and a decorative line has no contrast floor (accessibility.definition).

steps.question: Which states get their own visible value?
steps.why: Pressed for touch.
Fast feedback on an ease-out. The brand's spring waits for the moments that deserve it.
Focus must show on vivid color.

steps.rule: The fill of the item the pointer or the keyboard is on, or whose submenu is open. A state shows on the item's background, one step from the surfaces it sits on: darker in light, and darker in dark too, as raised layers take the lighter step.
steps.pick: neutral.100, two steps darker than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.0), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band without lifting off the page. It skips neutral.50, the page canvas, so a menu item never matches the page behind it.
steps.darkPick: neutral.floor: We use the floor step, below the canvas, for the item under the pointer or the keyboard in dark, in order to mark it as a band on both surfaces it meets: 1.13:1 on surface.default and 1.37:1 on surface.raised, and 1.05:1 off the page. The fill does this by stepping darker, as raised layers took the lighter step; muted text still reads 7.59:1 on it. So the hovered row or menu item shows on cards and menus alike, because hover and focus have their own look (accessibility.roles) and the neutral ramp sets the steps (color.definition).
